author: Layton, Edwin T.; Pineau, Roger; Costello, John
title: “And I Was There”: Pearl Harbor and Midway — Breaking the Secrets
notes: Fleet intelligence officer to Kimmel and then to Nimitz, writing forty years later with a case to make about who was blamed for 7 December and who should have been; filed as a memoir for that reason, not as a study. It is the best-known statement of the argument that the fuel tanks and the repair yard were the targets that would have mattered, and the usual source for Nimitz's remark that destroying the oil would have prolonged the war by two years. **Not read.** Every Internet Archive copy is a lending copy; nothing is quoted from it here and no page is given. Bibliographic detail is from the Internet Archive's catalogue records of the W. Morrow printing, not from the item.
